justifications.c1: Several independent figures: BP £8k fine plus £320k clean-up (ENDS, search-confirmed), Esso ~£15.5k and Shell £30k leak cases, Tesco £8m, and PRA stock-loss examples of £4,455 to ~£27k per site per year; but most data are 2004–2009, the leak cases involve majors, and vendor savings claims (Edensure £15k) are discounted.
justifications.c2: Trade guidance says wetstock must be reconciled daily (Cameron Forecourts), losses run at 0.4–0.59% of volume (Forecourt Trader benchmarks), and one operator reported ~250 litres short per delivery; the Blue Book wording itself was not found.
justifications.c3: Daily manual reconciliation and a paid outsourced service are documented: 'most fuel retailers already subscribe' to SIR services, priced from ~£130 per site per month (Edensure, search-confirmed, late-2000s article); manual labour time is not quantified.
justifications.c4: Petroleum (Consolidation) Regulations 2014 certificates may carry record-keeping conditions (Falkirk), East Lothian's conditions are cited as requiring reconciliation or leak-detection records for 12 months (page found, clause not visible in search), and EA has prosecuted forecourt leaks (BP, Esso, Shell, Tesco); no prosecution for missing wetstock records was found.
justifications.c5: Independents run ~5,300 of ~8,300 UK forecourts (The Grocer), but these include large groups like MFG (900+ sites), and no evidence was found on single-site owner-operators, their numbers or their spend.
justifications.c6: Only trade-association events sponsored by equipment vendors (PRA roadshows, APEA bulletin) and a Suresite and Leighton O'Brien deal; no site-visiting maintenance contractor reselling wetstock services was found.
justifications.c7: Crowded and served: Suresite, Gilbarco Insite360 (BP's 300+ sites), DFS/Fairbanks (EG Group), Edensure, Titan Cloud and Wolftank, with low-cost dealer deals and 'most retailers already subscribe'; the residual non-subscribing small independent is unsized.
justifications.c8: Veeder-Root TLS RS-232 report codes are documented (Chipkin, MSA), so a console bridge is feasible without ATEX, but the six-digit security code, single point-to-point port, other ATG brands and sites without ATGs are unresolved, and no BOM was gathered.
justifications.c9: Daily reconciliation and at least one licence condition requiring records for 12 months give a structural duty, and the market already pays monthly (Edensure ~£130 per site per month, well above £100 per site per year; Suresite three-year terms).
justifications.c10: Enforcement and environmental press (ENDS, EA release on Taw and Torridge), extensive trade press (Forecourt Trader, IEMA) and an operator's short-delivery account in trade press; no forum or review complaints were found.

weakest: The market is already served: trade press says most retailers subscribe to SIR services from established vendors, and the non-subscribing small independent niche is unsized and has no channel.
